title: The spine inclusion is inner anodyne
statement: Use the small simplicial sets, standard simplices and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For every integer $n\geq0$, let $\operatorname{Sp}[n]\subseteq\Delta^n$ be the simplicial subset whose $r$-simplices are the weakly increasing maps $\sigma:[r]\to[n]$ satisfying $\sigma(r)\leq\sigma(0)+1$. An inner fibration is a simplicial map having the right lifting property against every inclusion $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $0<i<m$. A map is inner anodyne if it has the left lifting property against every inner fibration: every commutative square with that map on the left and an inner fibration on the right admits a diagonal filler. The inclusion $\operatorname{Sp}[n]\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne.

source.place: Kerodon Example 1.5.7.7 (The Spine of a Simplex), assertion (a); the displayed definition of Spine[n] is used literally. Kerodon tag 00JA, distinct from the unrelated Stacks tag 00JA. Online source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$. A weakly increasing map $[m]\to[n]$ factors uniquely as a surjection onto its ordered image followed by the strictly increasing enumeration of that image. Thus a nondegenerate simplex of $\Delta^n$ is exactly a nonempty subset $S=\{a_0<\cdots<a_r\}\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and every simplex is a uniquely determined degeneracy of one of these. Put $\ell(S)=a_r-a_0$. For $k\geq1$ let $L_k$ contain the simplices of span at most $k$. Precomposition can only shrink the image, so these are simplicial subsets. The definition of the spine gives $L_1=\operatorname{Sp}[n]$ and $L_{\max(1,n)}=\Delta^n$. When $n=0$ or $1$ the spine already equals the simplex.

source.place: Proof, length filtration before the normalized-simplex argument Specialized to the directed line of Kerodon 00HL/00JA; the finite-subset calculation is written out here.

proof.text: Fix $2\leq k\leq n$. Call a nondegenerate simplex $S$ of span $k$ normalized when its first two vertices are $a,a+1$, where $a=\min S$. Such a simplex has dimension at least two. Removing its second vertex gives $T=S\setminus\{a+1\}$, a nonnormalized simplex of the same span. Conversely every nonnormalized simplex $T$ of span $k$ has at least two vertices and second vertex strictly larger than $\min T+1$; inserting $\min T+1$ gives a unique normalized simplex $S$. These operations are inverse, and the removed vertex has index $1$.

source.place: Proof, normalized simplices and observation (iii) Specialized to the directed line of Kerodon 00HL/00JA; the finite-subset calculation is written out here.

proof.text: For $1\leq r\leq n$ define $A_{k,r}$ to contain $L_{k-1}$, the normalized simplices of span $k$ and dimension at most $r$, the nonnormalized simplices of span $k$ and dimension at most $r-1$, and all their degeneracies. This is a simplicial subset: an endpoint face has smaller span; an inner face of a nonnormalized simplex remains nonnormalized; an inner face of a normalized simplex stays normalized unless its index is $1$, in which case it is nonnormalized and its dimension drops by one. Therefore $A_{k,1}=L_{k-1}$, and the bijection in step 2 gives $A_{k,n}=L_k$: every nonnormalized simplex of span $k$ is the second-vertex face of a normalized simplex of dimension at most $n$.

source.place: Proof, observations (i)-(iii) and definition of X(r) Specialized to the directed line of Kerodon 00HL/00JA; the finite-subset calculation is written out here.

proof.text: For $2\leq r\leq n$ attach one $\Delta^r$ for each normalized $r$-simplex $S$ of span $k$. Its endpoint faces lie in $L_{k-1}$, and every inner face except $d_1S$ is normalized of dimension $r-1$, hence already in $A_{k,r-1}$. Both $S$ and $d_1S$ are absent there: the first has normalized dimension $r$ and the second nonnormalized dimension $r-1$. Every proper face of $d_1S$ is present, since it either has smaller span or is nonnormalized of dimension $r-2$. Thus the intersection of this simplex with $A_{k,r-1}$ is exactly $\Lambda^r_1$. Different $S$ have distinct missing faces by step 2; their new simplices do not overlap. The unique surjection-image factorization in step 1 shows that their new degenerate simplices do not overlap either. Consequently maps from $A_{k,r-1}$ and these copies of $\Delta^r$ agreeing on the horns glue uniquely degree by degree. The glued maps commute with each simplicial operator: on an old simplex this holds for the given map on $A_{k,r-1}$, and on a simplex in an attached cell it holds for the given map on that copy of $\Delta^r$; agreement on the horn makes the two descriptions identical wherever both apply. This gives the pushout formula $A_{k,r}=A_{k,r-1}\amalg_{\coprod_S\Lambda^r_1}\coprod_S\Delta^r$. This also proves the formula when the indexing set is empty.

source.place: Proof, displayed normalized-simplex horn pushout, with its intersection and uniqueness checks Specialized to the directed line of Kerodon 00HL/00JA; the finite-subset calculation is written out here.

proof.text: An inner horn inclusion $\Lambda^r_1\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$ has the left lifting property against every inner fibration directly by that definition; here $r\geq2$, so $0<1<r$. For fixed $k,r$, the indexing set in step 4 is finite. Order it arbitrarily and attach its simplices one at a time. The intersection calculation in step 4 remains true after earlier attachments because distinct cells have disjoint new simplices. Thus each attachment is a pushout of this inner horn inclusion. Apply [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] to the category of small simplicial sets and the class $T$ of all inner fibrations. Its pushout and composition clauses make each $A_{k,r-1}\hookrightarrow A_{k,r}$ inner anodyne, and finite composition first over $r$ and then over $k$ makes $\operatorname{Sp}[n]=L_1\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ inner anodyne. Empty attachment lists use its identity clause. For $n=0,1$, the spine and simplex are equal, so this identity clause applies directly. This is the required left lifting property against every inner fibration.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NI-6b0581361 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement (Sp[n] = simplices with σ(r) ≤ σ(0)+1; inner anodyne = LLP against inner fibrations; any n ≥ 0) is unchanged and self-contained. Kerodon 00JA and 00J6 are not in literature/, so I could not open them here: WANTED is recorded, proof_origin is agent, and the proof stands on its own. Step 1: unique factorization through the image, so nondegenerate simplices are nonempty subsets; L_1 = Sp[n] and L_max(1,n) = Δ^n. Step 2: inserting or removing min+1 is a bijection between normalized and nonnormalized simplices of span k ≥ 2, with face index 1. Step 3: I checked closure of A_{k,r} under every face type, A_{k,1} = L_{k-1}, and A_{k,n} = L_k (a nonnormalized simplex misses a+1, so its dimension is ≤ n-1). Step 4: the faces of Δ^S outside A_{k,r-1} are exactly S and d_1S, so the intersection is Λ^r_1. Different cells do not overlap outside A_{k,r-1}; I checked directly that any S' ⊇ d_1S with S' ≠ S has span > k or is not normalized. Step 5: the inner horn is in llp(inner fibrations) by definition. Sequential pushouts and finite composition then follow from the identity, composition and pushout clauses of the Mathlib leaf lem-coef-lifting-class-closure, which I checked against LiftingProperty.lean:35-77. It needs no hypotheses on the category or the class and is a tool, not a route step, so no tool_uses entry is needed. Small cases n=0..3 were checked by hand; my own sequential-attachment enumeration for n ≤ 10 passed every horn-intersection, stage and final-equality check. The parent lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine uses exactly this statement. The rg duplicate search for spine/Segal/00JA/00J6/inner anodyne found no node stating the result. The blueprint from.place under thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale's opening compactification sentence is accurate. No new nodes, no SGA, no fixes.
